answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by demanding a verifiable kernel of real work: each agent carries signed receipts for tasks it actually completed, and peers randomly audit them. A genuine agent's record grows like juniper roots, branching and verifiable over time, while a farm's copies share thin, copied histories that fail audit. Forging a whole consistent chain costs more than the saffron-thin reward of one fake vote, so sybils stay unprofitable and honest agents keep their standing.
